title: Architecture Without an Architect? Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence in a Divided World
abstract: arXiv:2610.01716v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence presents an unusually difficult problem for global governance. The technology develops rapidly, crosses borders easily, and is shaped by actors whose resources and capabilities may rival those of states. Yet international responses remain fragmented, unevenly representative, and overwhelmingly non-binding. The challenge is therefore not simply to identify appropriate rules or institutions, but to understand who has the capacity and incentive to create, enforce, and adapt them.   This review essay examines these questions through Matthijs Maas's Architectures of Global AI Governance. Maas offers an ambitious framework for thinking about AI governance through the lenses of sociotechnical change, governance disruption, and regime complexity. translated_title: 没有建筑师的架构？分裂世界背景下的人工智能全球治理
translated_abstract: 人工智能给全球治理带来了一个异常棘手的难题。这项技术发展迅速，可以轻易跨越国界，并且受到那些资源和能力可能足以与国家相抗衡的行为者的塑造。然而，国际社会的应对措施仍然碎片化、代表性不均衡，且绝大多数不具约束力。因此，挑战不仅在于确定适当的规则或制度，更在于理解谁有能力和动力去创建、执行和调整这些规则。本评论文章通过马蒂亚斯·马斯的《全球人工智能治理的架构》一书来审视这些问题。马斯提供了一个雄心勃勃的框架，通过社会技术变革、治理颠覆和机制复杂性三个视角来思考人工智能治理。他的论述有效地避免了技术决定论和对单一制度蓝图的追求，转而强调碎片化且不断演变的可能性……
tldr: 这篇书评认为，人工智能全球治理的核心挑战不在于设计何种规则或制度，而在于理解在一个分裂的世界中，谁有能力和动力去创建、执行并调整这些治理架构。
en_tdlr: This review essay argues that the core challenge of global AI governance lies not in designing the right rules or institutions, but in understanding who has the capacity and incentive to create, enforce, and adapt them in a divided world.
